Further sulfur is generated after acid replenishment; account for SO2/bisulfite acidity rather than imposing an oversimplified fixed proton ceiling.

cases.title: A product-rich mixture tests the reverse ester equilibrium
cases.original_physical_forecast: With a product-rich initial reaction quotient, a reversible ideal-equilibrium implementation should move toward hydrolysis and produce more acid and ethanol.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Acid and ethanol increase while ester and water are consumed in the reverse stoichiometric direction.
If the command only supports forward extent, record a reverse-route limitation instead of calling no conversion an equilibrium success.

cases.title: Acidifying a saponification product does not automatically remake ester
cases.original_physical_forecast: Acidification shifts acetate toward acetic acid. Without a new esterification request, that protonation is not itself evidence of ester re-formation.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: The acetic-acid fraction increases after acid addition.
Separate proton-transfer changes from any actual C–O bond-forming esterification; no automatic reversed saponification is assumed.

cases.title: Follow carbon through esterification and alkaline cleavage
cases.original_physical_forecast: Ester made in the first transformation is cleaved in the second; initially unreacted acid also consumes part of the hydroxide budget.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Compute carbon across acid/acetate, ethanol and ester before and after both transformations.
Do not assign all added base to ester cleavage: neutralisation of residual acetic acid is a separate demand.

cases.title: Finite oxygen limits the requested respiration extent
cases.original_physical_forecast: The total available oxygen, including trapped air, is insufficient for the full glucose dose; the requested aerobic transformation should leave glucose.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Bound glucose consumption by measured pre-command total O2 divided by six.
Do not invent anaerobic products or assume that only the explicitly added oxygen was available.

cases.title: More theoretical stages change enrichment at the same cut specification
cases.original_physical_forecast: The modelled multi-stage separation should enrich the more volatile component more strongly than a one-stage separation of a matched feed.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare product compositions at equal cut fractions from the split feed.
No extra ethanol is created by increasing stage count; inventory closure includes both residues.

cases.title: Reduction changes whether iodine can be extracted into hexane
cases.original_physical_forecast: Reducing iodine to ionic iodide diminishes the neutral iodine available for transfer to the organic phase.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: First verify the redox conversion in the reduced feed.
The organic receiver from the reduced feed should contain less oxidised iodine than the matched unreduced control; sum all iodine species in both phases.

cases.title: Chromatography distinguishes dissolved neutral solutes without consuming the sample
cases.original_physical_forecast: The supported chromatography model can report differing retention behaviour for neutral solutes while leaving the vessel’s macroscopic inventory unchanged.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Require identified supported peaks and distinguish absent model parameters from absence of a compound.
Before/after inventories are unchanged by the analytical measurement; reported relative peak area is not automatically a calibrated mass fraction.

cases.title: Equal solute molality does not mean equal freezing-point depression
cases.original_physical_forecast: The electrolyte produces a larger ideal particle-count effect than the same amount of a molecular nonelectrolyte, depressing the freezing equilibrium more strongly.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare actual phase temperatures and dissolved particle inventories in the two mixed-phase states.
Do not impose exactly a factor of two once ion activities and freeze concentration become significant.

cases.title: A nonvolatile solute elevates a boiling plateau
cases.original_physical_forecast: When both cases are boiling, the saline solution should have a slightly higher phase-equilibrium temperature than pure water at the same external pressure.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Verify actual vapour production before calling either final temperature a boiling point.
Compare plateaus and salt ownership, allowing concentration to increase as water evaporates.

cases.title: Hydration state changes dissolution heat and water bookkeeping
cases.original_physical_forecast: Anhydrous copper sulfate and its pentahydrate provide the same copper/sulfate loading but different hydration-water and dissolution-enthalpy contributions.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: The pentahydrate contributes five waters per formula unit to the material balance.
Compare thermal changes against each initial-water baseline; the anhydrous salt is expected to warm more, subject to the declared enthalpy data.

cases.title: A molecular solid shows a melting plateau
cases.original_physical_forecast: A modest energy pulse can bring naphthalene to its modelled melting point and partly melt it instead of producing the full sensible-heat temperature rise.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Look for coexistence of solid and liquid naphthalene near the declared transition temperature.
Total naphthalene inventory is conserved except for any explicitly represented volatile loss.

cases.title: Pure acetic acid can freeze above water’s freezing point
cases.original_physical_forecast: Pure acetic acid can enter a solid/liquid coexistence region near its declared melting point, well above 0 C.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Confirm a phase change of acetic acid rather than formation of water ice.
The final temperature is compared with the registry transition of the pure substance, not vinegar or an aqueous acid solution.

cases.title: A metal absorbs latent heat while melting without being oxidised
cases.original_physical_forecast: The pulse can bring zinc to its melting region and partly melt it; a solid/liquid transition is not by itself a change in oxidation state.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Identify metallic zinc in both phases near its declared melting transition.
Any oxide formation must have its own oxygen source and reaction accounting; melting alone cannot create ZnO.

cases.title: Distinguish a common-ion effect from a background-electrolyte effect
cases.original_physical_forecast: Chloride changes silver-chloride equilibrium through common-ion and complexation effects; nitrate mainly changes the ionic medium. Equal salt amounts do not make the effects equivalent.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare total dissolved silver and free silver activity separately in all three vessels.
In this modest-chloride range, common-ion suppression should exceed the nitrate-only change; note any competing soluble complexes.

cases.title: Solvent identity changes the route to a silver-chloride precipitate
cases.original_physical_forecast: AgCl formation in water uses aqueous speciation, whereas the documented pure-ethanol route is constrained by dissolved reagent fractions and a curated metathesis rule.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Check for AgCl in both systems and explicitly distinguish undissolved starting salt from precipitated product.
Report actual conversion instead of assuming equal yields merely because equal formula amounts were added.

cases.title: The same inert-gas addition behaves differently at fixed pressure
cases.original_physical_forecast: With a materially closed, expanding regulated headspace, inert-gas addition expands the gas volume and can lower CO2 partial pressure, favouring CO2 transfer out of solution.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Pressure stays near the setpoint while headspace volume expands.
Track carbon conservation and any decrease in dissolved-carbon fraction; do not assume regulation vents mass.

cases.title: Salt can alter gas solubility without consuming the gas
cases.original_physical_forecast: Chemical expectation: a concentrated salt medium can reduce molecular CO2 solubility through salting-out; it does not stoichiometrically consume CO2.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare neutral dissolved CO2 separately from bicarbonate/carbonate and gas-phase carbon.
If the partition model lacks a salinity correction, record the missing effect as unsupported rather than forcing an expected difference.

cases.title: Enzyme saturation makes the substrate response sublinear
cases.original_physical_forecast: The Michaelis-type catalyst model predicts a less-than-proportional increase in initial reaction rate as peroxide concentration approaches or exceeds its saturation scale.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Calculate initial peroxide concentrations from actual liquid volumes, not from water volume alone.
The ratio of early absolute peroxide-consumption rates is smaller than the ratio of initial substrate concentrations.

cases.title: Requesting the same ester equilibrium twice must not create more matter
cases.original_physical_forecast: After equilibrium is reached, an identical second request should leave the reaction extent essentially unchanged rather than apply another fixed fractional conversion.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare every acid/alcohol/ester/water amount between the two equilibrium snapshots.
Allow solver tolerance, but not repeated net creation of ester without a changed reaction quotient.

cases.title: An energy-budgeted distillation is not a chosen mass fraction
cases.original_physical_forecast: The larger specified energy budget should generally collect more material, but composition and phase enthalpies prevent treating energy as a fixed mass fraction.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare collected amount and remaining feed in the two energy-limited cases.
Read the runtime energy-boundary explanation; do not assume all supplied joules go solely into latent heat.
